# Benzene

> UK grid connection intelligence from primary public sources. Benzene tells developers, land and planning advisers, lawyers and investors whether a site can connect to the grid and when, using NESO's connection register and the planning and contract records around it. Every figure is labelled confirmed, reported or inferred.

## What Benzene does

- A free interactive map of Britain's transmission connection queue: https://www.benzene-group.com/queue-map.html
- A free list of every change between NESO register files (projects joining, leaving or moving their connection date): https://www.benzene-group.com/changes.html
- A free weekly briefing on what changed in the underlying data, with sources
- Fixed-fee screening reports on a specific site or project (£1,950 fixed, one site, 5 working days), checking the connection queue, the wait, competing projects, and the planning and revenue-contract records

Research is produced with AI systems that read primary sources directly, and every report is reviewed before it is sent. Benzene reports what public records say. It does not provide engineering, legal or investment advice.

## Gate 1 and Gate 2

Under NESO's connections reform, Gate 2 projects receive a confirmed connection date, a confirmed connection point and a secure place in the reordered queue. Gate 1 projects receive only an indicative date and location. Source: https://www.neso.energy/news/connections-reform-key-unlocking-gb-growth

## Selected figures

All figures below are confirmed. Register figures are Benzene's analysis of the NESO TEC Register file of 16 November 2026, transmission connections only.

- Capacity waiting to connect: 592.1 GW in 1,677 unbuilt projects at 1,038 sites. 81.8 GW is connected.
- Capacity-weighted average wait to the contracted connection date: 6.7 years.
- 75% of waiting capacity has a contracted date of 2031 or later.
- Marked Gate 2: 136 projects, 25.4 GW, average wait 1.5 years. Marked Gate 1: 926 projects, 333.0 GW, average wait 8.1 years. Gate field blank: 615 projects, 233.6 GW.
- September 2026 balancing costs: £541m, of which about £390m was constraint costs. NESO's month-ahead forecast was £306m. Source: https://www.neso.energy/bsuos-outturn-september-2026
- Gate 2 Phase 1 offer deadline: Ofgem agreed on 2 October 2026 to extend it from 30 September to 31 October 2026 (its second extension). Gate 2 Phase 2 offers stay due by 31 January 2027. We have not yet seen a NESO statement that every Phase 1 offer was issued. Source: https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/transparency-document/ofgem-agreement-alternative-gate-2-whole-queue-g2twq-timetable

## Status tags

- Confirmed: read directly from a named primary source
- Reported: from a named secondary source, not yet confirmed at source
- Inferred: a deduction from confirmed data, with the reasoning shown

## Products and pricing

- Queue map and weekly briefing: free
- Free substation check: queued capacity, Gates and dates at any substation, reply within one business day
- Screening report: £1,950 fixed, one site, 5 working days. If it does not answer the brief, the client does not pay
- Data centre power brief: £2,950 fixed for up to three sites (£1,950 for one), 7 working days. Compares candidate sites for a large demand connection: transmission queue, local demand headroom, nearby generation and Ofgem's proposed data centre commitment fee at the requested size. Not an engineering study or legal advice. Sample: https://www.benzene-group.com/sample-data-centre-brief.html
- Landowner grid note: £495 fixed, one site, 3 working days. A two-page note for land agents and landowners pricing an option on how crowded the grid is near the land. Not a valuation or advice on option terms. Sample: https://www.benzene-group.com/sample-landowner-note.html
- Transaction Due Diligence: £3,950, 4 weeks. A desk-based review of public registers on named projects, not an engineering or legal review
- Site Selection Sprint: £6,450, 8 weeks
- Queue watch: £99 a month per watched site, five sites for the price of four. An email after each new NESO register on what changed at those sites
- Annual Intelligence Subscription: £15,600 a year
